title: Understanding The Keys Of The Kingdom
paragraphs: Since the beginning of January this year, we have started teaching this series about the Kingdom of God. I'm still in the introduction stage. And seven months of introductions have not even touched upon the essence of this wonderful and most important subject. It is the most important topic, the Kingdom of God. Today in this session we will focus on the statements Jesus referred to when he spoke about the kingdom having keys. I think it is very important to note that it is a plural word.

He did not say, "I will give you the key to the kingdom." This is not written anywhere in the four Gospels. Rather, he said: “I will give you the keys, in the plural, to the kingdom,” and this is extremely important. As we look at this Kingdom theme, which we will be focusing on throughout the week, I think Heaven is probably more excited today and during this week than it ever has been about this ministry.

We have held tremendous conferences and wonderful summits in the past, but I don't think they have stirred heaven's excitement more than this, because I believe we are focusing on what God always wants us to focus on, which is the Kingdom of God. Amen. There is nothing in the world more annoying than focusing on trivial matters. I think the church has become adept at focusing on secondary matters.

In fact, we have become a global organization that sells the benefits of a product without people understanding what that product is. For example, we sell faith to get things. This is the basis of the focus of this recent revivalist group known as the charismatic movement. We have become interested in the things in that movement. We focus on material benefits, and therefore we serve God primarily to obtain things.

This is why faith has become so important to that movement, because faith is one of the commodities or the currency used in the kingdom to benefit from it. Therefore, we focus on currency and interest, not on the kingdom itself. Jesus had to correct the disciples one day when they began to focus on the same thing. They began to focus on the things they said: "What do we eat? What do we drink? What do we wear? How do we live?" And then he stopped them. He told them, "Stop worrying." This is not fate.

This is worrying. He said, "Okay." Then he corrected their misconceptions. He said, " First seek the kingdom. Strive to understand the kingdom and embrace it." And if you do that, then all these things that have become your religion will follow as a consequence. It does not become the focus of attention. Instead, they become natural benefits. I would like to use the term natural benefits. In fact, if you want to get wet, just get in the water. Don't pray for wetness. Just get in the water. This is good.

If you want to burn, just go into the fire. You don't need to pray for the heat. Just go into the fire. And so is the kingdom. The kingdom is like entering an environment where what you desire happens naturally. The problem is that we don't even know this thing. And those of you who have been with me during the past six months, I hope you will never forget, and you young people, including my son there in the back, that handsome young man who has just returned from Jamaica. He is a evangelist now. Thank God.

I am very proud of him. I was proud of him to myself last night. Everyone needs to learn about the kingdom and then learn how it works. This is the core of the principle that Jesus presents, which truly speaks to the mechanisms of the Kingdom. Let's read some texts to introduce the topic of the Kingdom. I will use the board to take notes if you wish. Therefore, please take advantage of this opportunity to write down the most important messages. It is the message concerning the Kingdom of God.

Luke tells some detailed things about the kingdom. In Luke chapter four, we find some statements that I think are helpful. Let's read what Luke says. Ah, when you read this, I hope you will realize Jesus' focus. Luke says: “But Jesus said, ‘I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns, because that is why I was sent.’ Read aloud together, all of you.” Let's pause here for a minute. I was telling my colleagues at the end of this week that this really is this.

I have gained a deeper understanding of the Kingdom and I am beginning to realize its true power. But what really amazed me was this verse. This verse contradicts all the other things we were preaching, meaning that Jesus did not really come to preach healing. Look at the verse. He did not even come to preach about the resurrection. He did not come to preach miracles. He did not really come to preach about Calvary and the cross. He didn't even come to announce his death.

Actually, you might find it interesting, but listen carefully to what I'm about to say because you'll miss the point. Jesus never told the crowds about his death. I have read all four Gospels in the past six months. I read the four Gospels eleven times. Nowhere in those four Gospels did Jesus make a public announcement of his death. Once he hinted at it, and it was through a subtle gesture. He said, " Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up." He was referring to his resurrection.

But he never preached the message of Calvary to the people. Why? He only spoke about it privately with his students. Why? Because Calvary... Father, help me with this. This is not a religious message, but this statement will shake your faith. Jesus did not consider the message of Calvary a public matter. Let me ask you a question. If you own a shop and sell shoes, the key to the door is not of public interest. I'll say it again. If you own a store, you are in the shoe business. What do you want to sell? Shoes.

It's not the key that opens the door. Well, I haven't grasped your idea yet. I am speaking at a level higher than your comprehension. You don't stand on TV for sixty seconds to announce the key. This is correct. In other words, the method of entering the store is not your issue. This is correct. What they sell are shoes. You are in the shoe business. This is correct. So, you are advertising shoes. She talks about prices.

She talks about comfort, utility, how your shoes are better than other people's shoes, and that these shoes do not wear out. I mean, you really make the business thrive. You talk about shoes, and you don't even talk about the door. Once they find the store, they can enter through the door. Jesus never said that he was the store. Rather, he said, "I am he." We will deal with that in a few weeks. We have made the door the shop. Good. He says, "I came to preach one thing." He says, "That's why I came."

Let everyone say: "Why?" Say it out loud. What have you learned about "why"? Does the word "why" mean purpose in Hebrew and Greek? He says: "I came for one purpose, which is to preach the Kingdom of God." This is a difficult message to preach. And every Sunday I feel labor pains when I know this. Good? Many of you members have begun to see my contractions. Good. Because sometimes I stop and wonder, why? Because I remove the outer layers of religion. This is difficult. Good.

How do you get rid of things you've believed in for the past fifty years? Jesus came to do that, to preach the kingdom of God. Let's look at another verse that I considered very important in Luke 12:32. It says: "Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has..." What? " He was pleased to give you not a religion, but the kingdom. " First, he says: "The whole motivation for my coming and the whole reason for my coming is to do what?" "To preach the good news."

The word Gospel means the good news of the Kingdom, not a religion. Then he says, “ My Father’s good pleasure is to give you this kingdom.” Let me ask you a question. What does the word "pleasure" or "joy" mean? What do you mean? It means satisfaction. This means that God will never be satisfied until you receive the Kingdom of God, understand it, act upon it, and benefit from it. Everything else is not pleasing to God. So, God may have been completely dissatisfied for 1800 years or perhaps even longer.

The Church is only 2000 years old, born 2000 years ago in Jerusalem when the Holy Spirit came. I believe that during the first 300 years or so, or perhaps even the thousand years that followed, they still had a firm vision of the Kingdom. But remember that they were suffering too. Could it be that God never found a generation that fully understood that? Is my speech beyond your comprehension? You are all very lucky to be listening to me, and I know this. I am not arrogant, but let me tell you something.

In the Book of Acts, chapter one, the disciples have not yet grasped the matter. He said to them, and they said, "Will you establish the kingdom now?" They were thinking of overthrowing Caesar. The Bible says that he seated them again after the resurrection and explained to them again the kingdom of God. And he won't tell you what he did. And it doesn't tell you how long that seminar lasted. Let's go. They have n't grasped it yet. I believe the only person who truly understood the kingdom was not Peter, but Paul.

This is why the Bible very clearly states Paul's words: "I have been allowed to see things which the prophets who came before me never saw." When Peter met Paul, he said, "My God, this man is crazy, but what he says is the truth." He says, "I do n't understand everything he says, but listen to this man." Because the kingdom of God is still not understood. We continue to transform God's government into a religion. We continue to reduce the kingdom of God to an organizational club called religion.

Christ is not interested in religion. He came to bring a kingdom. Let me tell you why this interests me so much. Because in Matthew 25, read this verse with me. It says: “Come,” verse 20, verse 34, “you who are blessed by my Father, take the inheritance.” " What is your inheritance?" The kingdom, how long has it existed? Prepared for you since the founding of the world. Yes. Yes. This is in your holy book. In Matthew, quoting Jesus. Jesus said, " Your inheritance is not... my God." Oh, my God.

I must be careful about what I say because these tapes will spread throughout the world and I may be accused of heresy. I read the Bible, you know, I read the Bible. "But look, what you see and what you hear can be completely overridden by what you believe." The same spiritual turmoil you are experiencing now is the same turmoil that God put me through. If he has turned my world upside down, I will turn your world upside down. Good. I am talking about a state of holy chaos. Let's read the verse again.

Now, remember, forget your religion. I want you to read the verse. Look at the verse. Don't interpret it yourselves. Rather, they extracted the meaning from it. What are you saying? Come, my blessed father. In other words, if the Father blesses you, this is what He blesses you with. You will receive the inheritance. What is inheritance? An inheritance is something you rightfully own. Please write this down. The kingdom is rightfully yours. This means you have no right to belong to a religion.

You have no right to be Baptists. You have no right to be among the fifty-year-olds. You have no right to be Catholics. You have no right to be Sabbateans. You have no right to belong to the Church of God or the Prophecy. You have no right to belong to the Apostolic Church of God. You have no right to belong to anything. The only right you possess is the Kingdom of God. Amen. Amen. This is why sectarianism corrupts us. We worship religion. We do not worship God. We protect the religion.

We do not protect the gift of our heritage. We defend our organizations and our religion. We are not defending the Kingdom of God. This is our heritage. The following phrase says: "It has been prepared for you." since when? Since the creation of the earth. The Kingdom of God has always been God's idea. That's what that phrase means. That is why you were created. He created his children to inherit the kingdom of God. But what is the kingdom of God? This is from Revelation 5:10, a weighty verse.

She says: "And you have made us a god and a kingdom of priests to serve our god, and they will reign on the earth." Oh my God, I'm feeling stressed again. Religion puts us in heaven, but it all ends up on earth. Now, don't miss this, guys. You have heard me say this for years, and some of you in this church still do not believe me. You think you will go to heaven and rest there for a billion years by the crystal river drinking grapes. Your religion has taught you that.

Actually, I'm going to say something very, very profound. The sky causes us more trouble on Earth than the Earth itself. Okay, don't misunderstand me. Do you know why a young man entered a crowded area in the center of Jerusalem, or rather in Tel Aviv, two days ago? With bombs strapped to his body. Listen to me carefully. He entered a shopping area and pressed the button on the bombs strapped to his body, tearing his body to pieces. Fifteen people died in this operation.

About one hundred others were stunned and injured, and the building was completely destroyed. This boy did that because someone told him that it would take him to a place called Heaven and he would live there forever. And you do that, my God. Good. Good. Look, religion takes you off the earth, but the kingdom puts you on the earth. Jesus said, and the disciples asked him, " What should we pray for?" Prayer means seeking God. What should we ask of God? What should we ask of God? What did he say?

“What is the most important thing we should ask of God?” Jesus answered them. He said, " What?" He must pray. He says: "When you want to appeal to God, you must first respect the judge."
